results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/national: ECI data on Special Intensive Revision and electoral roll digitisation.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reported that over 68% of enumeration forms for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls have been digitised across 12 States and UTs.
notes.fact_box: The SIR phase covers 50,97,44,423 electors across 12 entities including UP, Kerala, and Lakshadweep. As of November 27, 2025, 34,86,60,338 forms (68%) have been digitised, with the enumeration phase scheduled to conclude on December 4, 2025.

prelims_pointers.text: Total electors covered in the current SIR phase: 50,97,44,423
Digitisation status as of Nov 27, 2025: 68.03% of total forms
States/UTs in SIR: Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep
Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are responsible for data upload via dedicated apps
Lakshadweep achieved the highest digitisation rate at 99.9% as of Nov 2025

notes.mains_question: Discuss how the digitisation of electoral rolls contributes to the integrity of the democratic process and identify the logistical hurdles in achieving universal data coverage.
mains_dimensions: Data integrity: Reduction of duplicate entries and 'ghost voters' through real-time digital verification by BLOs
Digital divide: Disparity in digitisation rates between states like Lakshadweep (99.9%) and Uttar Pradesh (47.59%)
Logistical bottlenecks: Challenges in high-volume data upload in regions with poor internet connectivity or low digital literacy
